title: Creating Your First Script 📜
description: Put commands into a file and run it. Hello, world of scripting!

slides.title: What is a Script? 📝
slides.content:
## Script = Recipe
A script is just a text file containing a list of commands, like a recipe. Instead of typing commands one by one, you save them in a file and run them all at once.

- Files end with `.sh` by convention (not required).
- They can be run with `bash filename.sh` or made executable.

slides.title: Your First Script 🚀
slides.content: Create a file called `hello.sh` using the `touch` command (creates empty file) or an editor like nano.

quizData.question: What does `touch hello.sh` do?

options.text: Creates an empty file named hello.sh (or updates its timestamp)

quizData.explanation: `touch` creates an empty file if it doesn't exist, or updates the last-modified time if it does.

slides.title: Writing into the Script ✍️
slides.content:
## Using a Simple Editor

Use `nano`, `vim`, or even `echo` to write lines into your file.
For beginners, nano is easiest:
```
nano hello.sh
```
Inside, type:
```
echo "Hello, World!"
echo "Today is $(date)"
```
Save (Ctrl+O) and exit (Ctrl+X).

slides.title: Running with bash 🏃
slides.content: Use the `bash` command to run your script.

quizData.question: Type the command to run a script named `myscript.sh` using bash.
quizData.explanation: You can invoke a script with `bash myscript.sh`. This runs it even if the file isn't executable.

slides.title: Pro Tip 🚀
slides.content:
## Keep Learning Small
Save your script in a dedicated folder like `~/scripts`. It keeps things organized!
